newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq lower on profit-taking after new high.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq lower on profit-taking after new high.

text.p: Profit-taking and a weak bond market pulled the Nasdaq Composite lower on Tuesday, one day after it hit a record closing high.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was down 10.73 points, or 0.86 percent, at 1240.14 at its unofficial close while declines led advancing issues 2291 to 1821 on volume of about 578 million shares.

Semiconductor stocks, which led the market higher on Monday, gave up ground today after Salomon Brothers said it cut its rating on Intel Corp to hold from strong buy, citing high valuation and fourth quarter earnings concerns. Intel was down 3-1/8 at 101-5/8.

The high techs were mixed. Microsoft Corp was down 2-1/8 at 135-3/8. Iomega Corp, as active as ever, was up 1-3/4 at 23-5/8, Cisco Systems Inc was down 1-3/4 at 64-1/4 and Sun Microsystems Inc was up 1/8 at 65-3/4.

Canadian oil company Arakis Energy Corp topped the over-the-counter most active list, rising 29/32 to 4-6/32 after the company revealed it was drawing close to a possible deal with joint venture partners for development of its oil concession in Sudan.
